source: make a 3d game about clock people vs couchs and I want a giant high detail map and that will be the lobby I also want you to make platforms for which if you step on you teleport to another map and defend your base city that has 200 health also you can pick which difficulty you want to do with nightmare being the hardest and make a summon area on which you spend 100 counts to summon a unit the chances of the units are:common -75% rare-20% epic-3% legendary-0.9% mythic-0.1%

image_prompt.text: High walls and clutter across the defended ground so no single unit placement covers every approach
Structures around the base city that units and abilities can clear
The base city itself, built to read as the thing being defended and to show how much of its health is left
A giant, densely detailed lobby where players gather between runs
Physical platforms in the lobby, each clearly marked as the way into a different battle map
A summon area in the lobby where players spend currency to pull a unit

layout_placement.text: The base city as the primary health pool, defensible from every direction since units path across open ground rather than down one lane
Wave origins at the edges of the contested ground where attackers enter
Step-on platforms in the lobby paired to each separate battle map
A trigger on the summon area that opens the unit pull

notes: Shape was a close call between the enemy lane and open contested terrain. The prompt names a defended base with a health pool but never a path, so the cheaper shape was taken; if waves are meant to walk a fixed route this becomes lane-actor-track and P6.

The prompt asks for two builds — a giant lobby and the battle maps behind the platforms — and the handoff has one shape. The shape and most options describe the battle map, while the lobby, which is the part the user emphasised, is carried by two options only.

Numbers given by the user are lost: the base has 200 health, a summon costs 100 counts, and the rarity table is 75 / 20 / 3 / 0.9 / 0.1 percent. tracker-core is exactly the option for a health pool and cannot hold the number.
Who or what attacks the base is never stated; clock people versus couches is read as the two sides.

open_questions.ask: How giant is the lobby — a large plaza you can cross in half a minute, or a town-sized hub?
Do the couches attack the base in waves you survive, or is it a straight fight between the two sides?
Do attackers follow one fixed path to the base, or come from anywhere across open ground?

theme: Surreal object mascots — clock-headed figures against animate couches, high detail

coverage_missing.ask: How large should the lobby be?
What attacks the base, and in waves or continuously?
Fixed enemy path or open ground?
How many battle maps do the platforms lead to, and are they variations of one map or distinct places?

answers.ask: How giant is the lobby — a large plaza you can cross in half a minute, or a town-sized hub?
answers.answer: Make it a town-sized high-detail lobby hub.

answers.ask: Do the couches attack the base in waves you survive, or is it a straight fight between the two sides?
answers.answer: The couches attack the base city in waves, and players defend its 200 health.

answers.ask: Do attackers follow one fixed path to the base, or come from anywhere across open ground?
answers.answer: Use one fixed path leading to the base city so the defense gameplay is clear and playable.
